title: The candle that lost its green
scenario:
You make a winter web banner for a candle brand. The client wants warm evening light and an amber and deep-green look. The deep green on the jar label must match the brand file.

Your first prompt gave flat light and dull colours. Then you sent one edit message with four changes, and the label colour broke. The exhibit shows both rounds.
exhibit:
Brief
  Brand: Ember & Oak, hand-poured candles. Winter web banner.
  Look: warm evening light from the left, amber and deep green.
  The jar label (deep green) must match the brand colour file.

Prompt v1
  "A cozy candle on a table, moody lighting, nice warm colours"

What came back
  Flat, even light from the front. Brown and grey tones.
  Hard to tell the time of day.

Edit turn you sent (one message)
  "Make it warmer, make the jar deep green, darker background,
   and more dramatic."

What came back
  Warmer light, but the label turned orange-green.
  The shadows moved and the table texture changed.

questions.prompt: Which rewrite of prompt v1 follows the vendors' guides best?

options.text: "A candle on a table, extremely moody, atmospheric, cinematic and dramatic lighting, with a very cozy and warm winter feel."
options.explanation: These are mood words. OpenAI's guide says to specify scale, atmosphere and colour instead of relying on mood words alone.

options.text: "A candle on a table. No flat light, no front light, no grey tones, no cold colours, no dull look, no unclear time of day."
options.explanation: This lists what to avoid. The tip in the Gemini API docs is to describe the scene you want in positive words (chapter 1).

options.text: "A hand-poured candle on an oak table at dusk. Soft, warm window light from the left. Amber and deep green tones."
options.explanation: Right. It names the time of day, the quality, the source and the direction of the light, and the colours with quality words. The guides' examples are written this way.

options.text: "A candle on a table with the best, most perfect, award-winning, professional and stunning lighting and colours."
options.explanation: Praise words don't say where the light comes from or what colours you want.

questions.prompt: Your one-message edit changed four things, and the label broke. How should you run the next edits?

options.text: Send the same four changes again in capital letters, so the model sees they all matter.
options.explanation: Capital letters don't split the changes. You still can't tell which words broke the label.

options.text: Send one change per turn, and in each turn list what must stay, such as the label colour.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's guide says to request one change and repeat the details to preserve. Google also recommends small follow-up changes.

options.text: Start a new conversation for each change with no image, and write the whole scene again.
options.explanation: Without the image there is nothing to edit. The model makes a new picture and you lose what worked.

options.text: Add "be careful with the label" to the end of the same four-part message and resend it.
options.explanation: It is still four changes in one turn. OpenAI's guide says to request one change at a time.

questions.prompt: Now you only want warmer light. Which edit prompt fits the guides best?

options.text: "Make everything warmer. The light, the jar, the label, the table and the background should all feel like winter."
options.explanation: This asks for a colour change on every object, including the label you must protect.

options.text: "Make the light warmer, and adjust the colour grading to amber, and make the jar a deeper green at the same time."
options.explanation: This is a light change, a colour grading change and an object colour change in one turn.

options.text: "Warmer please. More cozy, more winter, more mood, more evening, more glow and more of everything else too."
options.explanation: Mood words don't say what to change and what to keep.

options.text: "Make the light warmer, like late sun from the left. Keep the label colour, the layout and the camera angle unchanged."
options.explanation: Right. One change, described as light you can see, plus a list of what must stay. OpenAI's guide lists camera angle among the details to keep for precise edits.

questions.prompt: The final label is close to the brand's deep green, but a colour picker shows it is off. What do you do?

options.text: Fix the label colour in your design tool, or composite the approved label in, instead of prompting again.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's guide says that if a region must stay pixel-identical, you should composite it instead of relying on prompting alone.

options.text: Add "exact brand green" three more times to the prompt and keep regenerating until it looks right.
options.explanation: A colour word is not a colour code. Repeating it does not make the model hit an exact value.

options.text: Accept it, because colour words in a prompt always give the exact brand colour after a few tries.
options.explanation: No guide promises an exact colour from words. OpenAI's guide says repeated edits can still change details you meant to keep.

options.text: Change the brand's colour file to match the model's green, so the banner and the brand file agree.
options.explanation: The brand file is the rule. The image must match it, not the other way round.
